I think we have to face the reality that Vtes will not receive any support*
from White Wolf unless it is done on volunteer time, that is none of us have
updated the demo so it will not be updated.

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
"David Wilson" <Wil...@vtes.org> wrote in message news:<lESjc.4640$Nz2....@news.itd.umich.edu>...


I'm just guessing here, but I'd think that the existence of the VTES
pages on White Wolf's webpage, including the graphic layout work, the
forum there, the effort to preview cards with actual card images, the
bandwidth and memory involved, etc etc is not actually entirely done
on a volunteer basis (as opposed to being done by paid employees on
company time.)

Though it does raise the (completely for me) curiousity-based question
of 'Does LSJ get paid for his efforts?' and 'Do the mythical design
team members get paid anything?'

(Also, note that while the online demo page has not been updated in
ages, White Wolf _has_ supported the idea of demoing the game lately
in a tangible form. As evidenced by the new demo decks with the
special set-emblem on every card, for example.)

-John Flournoy

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
John Flournoy wrote:
> Though it does raise the (completely for me) curiousity-based question
> of 'Does LSJ get paid for his efforts?' and 'Do the mythical design
> team members get paid anything?'

I am an independent contractor. WW pays me for my design work, my net.rep
work (answering a few questions here and there), and my work on the
/vtes portion of the web page.

Other designers are also compensated. The Rules Team (which is distinct
from the design team, at least in principle) receives no additional
compensation. Being mythical, though, they hardly have need for something
as mundane as coin. :-)

--
